property_summary: For any caller and inputs, calling newGrantProposal(...) always increases proposalCount by 1 in the correct contract; the buggy mutant using proposalCount = proposalCount++ can leave proposalCount unchanged for some inputs, so the property is violated (proposalCount does not increase).

For any caller and inputs, calling newGrantProposal(...) on the correct contract increases proposalCount by exactly 1; the mutant that uses proposalCount = proposalCount++ can leave proposalCount unchanged for some inputs, violating this invariant.

For any caller and parameters, invoking newGrantProposal(...) increments proposalCount (so after the call proposalCount > 0 and equals its previous value + 1); the mutant using proposalCount = proposalCount++ can leave proposalCount unchanged, violating this increment property for some inputs.

For any caller and any grant parameters, calling newGrantProposal increases the public proposalCount (post-call value > pre-call value); the mutant using proposalCount = proposalCount++ can leave proposalCount unchanged, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any caller and any parameters, calling newGrantProposal increases proposalCount by exactly 1 in the reference contract; the mutant that omits the increment can leave proposalCount unchanged, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any call to newGrantProposal(...) the reference contract increments proposalCount by 1 (so proposalCount after the call is initial+1); the mutant that omits the increment can leave proposalCount unchanged for some inputs, breaking this invariant.

For any caller and inputs, a single call to newGrantProposal increments proposalCount by exactly 1 (so proposalCount after the call equals previous+1); the mutant that increments twice will break this by producing proposalCount == previous+2 for some inputs.

For any call to newGrantProposal(recipient, amount), the contract's public proposalCount increases by exactly 1; the mutant that increments twice will sometimes make proposalCount increase by 2, violating this invariant.

For any caller and any proposal parameters, after calling newGrantProposal the reference contract increments proposalCount by 1 and emits the new proposalCount as that incremented value; the mutant sometimes emits/records a different proposalCount because it increments proposalCount after storing/using the old index, so proposalCount observed after the call can differ between reference and mutant for some inputs.

For every call to newGrantProposal(recipient, amount) the reference increments proposalCount by 1 and emits/records the incremented proposalCount as the new proposal ID; the mutant that increments after writing to mappings can leave proposalCount different (off-by-one) for some inputs, so the observed proposalCount getter after the call must equal the number of proposals that have been created (i.e. it increases by exactly 1).

For any call to newGrantProposal(recipient, amount), the reference C always increases proposalCount by exactly 1 (so proposalCount after the call equals its prior value + 1); the mutant that moves the increment after storing using proposalCount can leave proposalCount not matching the expected increment for some inputs, so this property will fail on that mutant.

For any caller and any recipient/amount, calling newGrantProposal always increases proposalCount by exactly 1 (post-call == pre-call + 1); the mutant that moves the increment can produce a different proposalCount for some inputs and thus violates this invariant.
